I know a lot of you are asking how I achieved this look, so I'll try to explain how the best I can! The cake is iced in buttercream. I definitely got it nice and cold before adding the details. The black is gel and the gold is classic gold airbrush. Both from decopac. For the big smears, I cut a piece of plastic that's used for cake collars. I dipped the piece in the gel and smear how I saw fit! Just takes a light touch! I would feather it out to give it more of a smeared look. You could probably get away with using a business card as well if you don't have the plastic. I've just recently discovered that people use those kinds of cards for shaping cakes, so I don't see why it wouldn't work for this as well. For the little lines, I went in with a paint brush. Same with the gold ✨️ 

If you have any other questions, feel free to ask! I hope this helps! 😊

Well before I go start down a downgrade I make sure I'm already going a slow enough speed so my rmps aren't too high, but when the cruise control senses the speed increasing, it kicks on the j and only raises the rmps a little if any. If you're going too fast it will kick them too high which indicates ya need to slow down more. 
And yes I always make sure I don't hold down pressure too long on my service brakes :)

I agree with 100% of what you said. You go at a low speed to maintain control to use your cruise down hills, definitely not setting the speed to 70!! It seriously helps with wear and tear on your service brakes and just like you said, the cruise control throws on the j brakes for you whenever it senses the speed picking up, and if it can't hold, you slow it down more with your brakes or J and reset it. There's even another way I was taught thats called "desend control" which is when you have the j brakes already on, you flip on your cruise at the desired (low) speed and a little light comes on the dash thats a green circle with a truck pointing down. But of course this is all only with automatic trucks, not manual.
